channel.title: AI Security Digest
channel.description: Curated AI security insights and articles from various sources

item.title: AI Threat Intelligence: 4 Emerging Threats Facing AI Agents
item.description:
Tags: ["AI Security", "Cybersecurity", "Threat Intelligence", "Artificial Intelligence"]
Summary:
  • AI agents face new threats like memory poisoning and model extraction.
  • Identity spoofing is a growing concern.
  • Multi-agent collusion increases attack complexity.
  • Proactive AI threat intelligence is essential.
  • It helps detect anomalies and simulate attacks.

item.title: ISO/IEC 42001: AI Management System Standard Explained
item.description:
Author: Fergal Glynn
Date: October 23, 2025
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "AI Governance", "Risk Management", "Ethical AI", "Standards and Compliance"]
Summary:
  • ISO/IEC 42001 is a new standard for AI management systems.
  • It provides a certifiable framework for ethical AI governance.
  • The standard helps manage risks like bias and security issues.
  • It promotes continuous oversight and compliance throughout the AI lifecycle.
  • Organizations can use it to build responsible AI policies.
  • The standard supports trust and accountability in AI deployment.

item.title: ISO/IEC 23894: AI Risk Management Standard Explained
item.description:
Author: Fergal Glynn
Date: October 23, 2025
Tags: ["AI Risk Management", "International Standards", "AI Governance", "Cybersecurity", "Compliance"]
Summary:
  • ISO/IEC 23894 is a voluntary international AI risk management standard.
  • It helps identify and mitigate AI-specific risks.
  • The standard complements other frameworks like ISO/IEC 42001 and NIST AI RMF.
  • It supports responsible and secure AI deployment.
  • Organizations can improve trust and compliance by following it.
  • The article also covers implementation best practices and challenges.

item.title: From word docs to data analysis: Evaluating AI agent performance across everyday apps
item.description:
Author: Dmitry Zubanov, Magdalena Konkiewicz
Date: October 1, 2025
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Human-Computer Interaction", "Software Testing", "Data Annotation", "Machine Learning Evaluation"]
Summary:
  • An AI company tested its agent's ability to use everyday computer applications.
  • Basic actions like clicking and typing were not enough.
  • They created thousands of realistic tasks across various software.
  • Human evaluators assessed task completion and handling of software quirks.
  • Quality control ensured consistent and accurate evaluations.
  • The project revealed strengths and weaknesses in real-world AI application use.

item.title: How Toloka helped poolside define and measure AI quality for developers
item.description:
Author: Mariya Shmatova, Mikhail Ostanin
Date: October 15, 2025
Tags: ["AI Evaluation", "Software Development", "Machine Learning Models", "Quality Assurance", "Developer Tools"]
Summary:
  • Poolside needed a way to measure AI answer quality beyond accuracy.
  • Toloka created a pairwise comparison evaluation framework.
  • The framework considers developer intent and task categories.
  • It provides consistent, context-aware assessments.
  • This helps identify model strengths and weaknesses.
  • Experts review answers to ensure clarity and usefulness.

item.title: Toloka podcast: How RL Gyms are redefining data for AI agents
item.description:
Author: Toloka Team
Date: October 21, 2025
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Reinforcement Learning", "Data Science", "Machine Learning", "AI Training Environments"]
Summary:
  • Toloka leaders discuss the shift from crowdsourced data to expert-led AI training.
  • Reinforcement learning (RL) Gyms create controlled environments for AI agents.
  • These gyms use verifiable rewards instead of static human feedback.
  • Private benchmarks often outperform public ones in AI training.
  • Achieving near-perfect data quality is costly but crucial.
  • The talk highlights collaboration between humans and machines in AI development.

item.title: Model Context Protocol: How to Reduce Security Risks in Enterprise AI Deployments
item.description:
Author: Andrija Dumančić
Date: Oct 21, 2025
Tags: ["Enterprise AI", "AI Security", "Model Context Protocol", "Cybersecurity", "AI Infrastructure"]
Summary:
  • MCP enables AI assistants to perform real-world actions using external tools.
  • It connects LLMs to APIs, databases, and system commands.
  • This increases enterprise AI usefulness but also raises security risks.
  • Common threats include prompt injection, tool poisoning, and command injection.
  • Enterprises must secure MCP workflows before deployment.
  • SPLX offers proactive red teaming to identify vulnerabilities.
